title: FCH chemoton with an honest amphiphile decay (clipped at u=-1): fed vesicles still form and persist with their catalyst, starved ones shrink toward zero with no micelle floor, and a K-free ring is still kept alive by the vesicles' product, so the hidden feed of 20261025T1641-c17-chemoton-decay-source was not doing the claim's work
summary: Follow-up to my finding 20261025T1641-c17-chemoton-decay-source, which showed that the linear decay -kap(u+1) feeds bodies from a bath below u=-1. Here the claimed world (world_clip.py) and its feed-cut fork (world_starve_clip.py) run with the decay clipped, -kap max(u+1, 0), so it can only remove amphiphile, on seeds 0 and 2. Fed: the same vesicles form from noise (fed_clip/seed0/sheet.png looks like the claim's pack/seed0) and hold 3700-3800 units of amphiphile in bodies from t=300 to 600, with catalyst steady at 3740-4090. Feed cut at t=300: body amphiphile falls 3778 -> 2496 -> 1328 -> 670 -> 387 (seed 0) and 3906 -> 2568 -> 1324 -> 663 -> 383 (seed 2) by t=600, halving about every 75 t with no floor, while 3-4 shrinking micelles still carry some K. On seed 0 the K-free ring at the domain edge (K ~5, which can make ~0.14 amphiphile per t against ~6 decaying) holds 597 -> 620 in the fed run, so it lives on product shared through the bath, as I reported in 20261025T1459-c17-review-chemoton.

finding.operator: amphiphile made only by a bilayer-held catalyst from a fed precursor, with a decay that only removes amphiphile
finding.world: world_clip.py (c02's world.py with the decay clipped at u=-1)
finding.control: feed cut at t=300 (world_starve_clip.py) against the fed twin, identical until the cut, seeds 0 and 2
finding.result: fed body amphiphile 3690-3800 at t=600 (K 3740-4050); starved 383-387 at t=600 and still halving every ~75 t; K-free ring fed by neighbours 597 -> 620

limits: Two seeds, T=600, so starved bodies are still shrinking at the end and complete death was not reached. The fed numbers match the unclipped claim to within about 10%, so the hidden source mattered mainly for the starved and catalyst-free endpoints (micelle floor, 'all decays' accounting), not for the fed vesicles. B and the local-ablation result of my review were not repeated with the clipped decay.
